title: Client intelligence and discovery
thesis: Begin with everything Actionist already knows, enrich it with bounded public business context, then ask only the questions needed to identify valuable workflows.
owns: Business links and bounded site reconnaissance
Stakeholders, systems of record and constraints
Conversation history and unresolved discovery questions
known: Actionist can pre-populate client context before chat
A generic “what app do you want?” prompt wastes known information
The useful target is a painful workflow and measurable outcome, not a feature wishlist
open: Which Actionist client fields are canonical?
What may be scraped automatically?
How do we distinguish stated wants from observed workflow pain?
What confidence threshold triggers a follow-up question?
agent: Map Actionist client context, define the discovery schema, question-selection policy and confidence model.
latest_findings: Discovery state should be deterministic and server-owned; the model owns phrasing, not truth.
Score access persistence and content sensitivity separately.
Use explicit qualify, prototype, disqualify and escalate terminal states.

title: Outcome and product specification
thesis: Translate business conversation into a small, testable ProductSpec before selecting repositories or UI.
known: 17 industries, 12 teams, 66 use cases, 72 ideas and 12 atoms are already catalogued
Requirements must remain implementation-independent
One valuable workflow is a better starting unit than an entire industry
open: What is the minimum ProductSpec?
How should assumptions and confidence be represented?
When should a prototype answer a question instead of more chat?
agent: Design the canonical outcome/product schema and prove it against five target workflows.
latest_findings: Elicit into a falsifiable ProductSpec with EARS-like slots and generated Gherkin.
Track UNCOVERED and NEEDS_CLARIFICATION explicitly with provenance.
Block progression on a client Accept/Revise gate; the five-workflow proving harness remains unrun.

title: Curated capability shelf
thesis: Hand-curate the first high-value software capabilities—Notion-like notes, Airtable-like data, calendar, CRM, support, files, approvals—before trying to automate the whole internet.
owns: Recommended reuse shape and supported archetypes
known: 500 OSS candidates and 118 commercial builder surfaces are already registered
Stars and metadata do not establish adaptation quality
SISOCRM proves that engines, product surfaces and infrastructure need different ownership choices
open: Which top 100 capabilities recur across the 17 industries?
What does quality mean per capability kind?
Should Notion/Airtable-like systems remain services, embedded modules or transplants?
How many complete systems versus small blocks belong in v1?
agent: Create a human-reviewed top-100 shelf ranked by client value, product quality, seam clarity and measured adaptation cost.
latest_findings: The 200-repo shelf resolves to 134 products, 20 frameworks and 46 primitives.
Product-basis supply is 13 commodity, 6 scarce, 3 product-layer-missing and 2 underdetermined.
Case/workflow, e-sign and field operations support “borrow the engine, build the product surface.”

title: Autonomous repo-to-block foundry
thesis: Automate source understanding, boundary extraction and adaptation evidence while keeping semantic reuse-shape decisions explicit and reviewable.
known: Phase 8 defined source shapes, stages and 23 negative paths
Full automation is the wrong target: shape choice and semantic adaptation need judgment
A repository can yield several blocks or no block
open: What can AST/runtime probes establish autonomously?
How do we detect hidden auth, settings and migration ownership?
What diff/adaptation budget predicts a bad candidate?
How is an upstream update replayed safely?
agent: Build the reusable conversion protocol and three worked traces: intact service, transplanted subsystem and extracted package.
latest_findings: A repository is a source container, not the reusable unit.
Choose service, module, transplant, package, adapter, pattern, template or custom-delta shape before extraction.
Identity, dependency closure and human shape choice precede normalization surgery.

title: Living UI component layer
thesis: Maintain a continuously refreshed, visually browsable component corpus where people and agents can find structural necessities and contextual inspiration.
owns: Taxonomy, tags and semantic use cases
known: Two complementary 21st-derived stores join to 8,515 identities
3,506 legacy entries are source-bearing while much of the newer harvest is preview/bundle oriented
Components range from universal necessities—navigation, forms, feedback—to contextual patterns
open: What is the canonical component taxonomy?
How are near-duplicates clustered visually and structurally?
Which components are required for every archetype?
How are new 21st.dev releases discovered and re-indexed?
What metadata helps a client visually choose without understanding component names?
agent: Design the component ingestion, taxonomy, dedupe, preview and visual-selection system; test it on navigation, hero, footer, table and form families.
latest_findings: The normalized local union is about 8,483 component identities; the source-bearing legacy store has 3,507 real components.
Replace inconsistent tags with canonical entities, aliases and measured visual clusters.
Own the archetype shell and core app primitives; harvest decorative surfaces. The layer is a snapshot, not yet living.

title: Design taste and preference learner
thesis: Learn a client’s visual preferences through a minimal sequence of high-information comparisons, separate from choosing individual components.
known: Prior research proposed contrast, radius, shadow, border, typography, density and chroma as mechanical knobs
Sequential galleries and Bradley–Terry/Luce models are relevant
Forced choices without “none” pollute the preference model
open: Is the mathematical minimum 7, 14 or another number of choices?
Which axes are independent?
Should choices use whole screens or controlled fragments?
How does preference confidence change by component context?
agent: Design and evaluate the active-learning experiment, including stopping rules and a reproducible DesignDNA output.
latest_findings: P06 established the adaptive learning mechanism, not the complete visual grammar.
Use controlled realistic screens, an outside option, per-dimension confidence and adaptive least-resolved-dimension targeting.
Learn continuous DesignDNA internally, but ship a complete pre-gated token pack; the exact axes, levels and 8–12 round estimate still require focused experiments.

title: Token and theme harmonizer
thesis: Preserve the quality of each imported capability while translating its visual assumptions into one semantic Actionist/client token system.
known: Blocks should consume semantic tokens rather than hard-coded brand values
Existing Teable work shows format conversion and scoped bridges are safer than blind aliasing
Taste profile and component selection are inputs, not the same artifact
open: How much donor visual identity should remain?
Can token mapping be inferred reliably?
How are unmapped bespoke CSS and canvas surfaces handled?
What score means two blocks look coherent?
agent: Define the semantic token contract and prove harmonization across three visually different imported surfaces.
latest_findings: Map donor variables into an Actionist semantic token contract rather than sharing raw CSS variables.
Re-render previews under the selected pack so the client only chooses reproducible designs.
Visual compatibility and scoped token bridges need tests across genuinely different donors.

title: Archetypes, shells and layouts
thesis: Reuse application-level workflow skeletons without forcing every product into one five-area dashboard.
owns: Case, portal, CRM, scheduling, finance, support and operations archetypes
known: Ten B2B archetypes have been identified
Case/workflow and portal demand are strong while clean template supply is thin
Generic admin/dashboard templates are abundant but weakly differentiated
The inherited five-area ISSO shell is only a hypothesis
open: Which archetypes cover 80% of the first 17 industries?
What is universal shell infrastructure versus archetype-specific UX?
Which side-nav variations should clients choose visually?
How does the shell absorb donor navigation?
agent: Define the first archetype contracts and visual shell variants; start with case/workflow and client portal.
latest_findings: Reject a universal five-area shell; Actionist owns a host frame while capability navigation varies by reuse shape.
Shopify and Atlassian prove the navigation boundary is a design choice, while the host visual contract is stable.
Five starting spines—case/workflow, field operations, learning/content, scheduling and CRM—cover most target industries.

title: Data and state plane
thesis: Standardize typed data capabilities and ownership—not one database implementation inside every block.
owns: State classification and source of truth
known: Postgres is a strong default for new owned transactional B2B data
Mature donor services should often retain native stores
One owner per table and migration is the strongest local rule
Cross-service views can use Actionist-owned event/read models
open: What operations must v1 data ports support?
One DB, schemas, service stores or hybrid per client?
How are dual writes prevented?
What migration/rollback contract belongs in an assembled release?
agent: Run a workload-driven data-plane bake-off across owned Postgres, donor API, event read model and local state.
latest_findings: Postgres is the default for Actionist-owned transactional data, not a universal donor invariant.
Enforce one authoritative owner per table and migration, with tenant identity from the first migration.
Use donor stores plus events/read models for intact services and real foreign keys for absorbed code.

title: Identity, settings and navigation host
thesis: Give every capability one Actionist identity, tenant, settings hierarchy and navigation surface while removing duplicate donor onboarding and account chrome.
known: Donor apps commonly bring their own auth, signup, settings and navigation
Replacing logos is trivial; replacing ownership boundaries is not
SISOCRM has partial host-session and route-mount precedents
open: What is Actionist’s canonical host contract?
Can settings/navigation be declarative?
Which donor routes must be unreachable?
How are capability permissions represented consistently?
agent: Define the host absorption contract and measure the real branding/auth/onboarding/settings/navigation delta on one mature donor.
latest_findings: The host owns authority: identity, tenant, URL space, navigation registry and settings provenance.
PackagingProfile selects federation versus absorption; there is no single integration pattern.
Identity has strong precedent, navigation partial precedent, and settings absorption is the largest unknown.

title: Connector and external-action plane
thesis: Reuse broad provider catalogues and OAuth/action mechanics while Actionist owns tenant-scoped connections, authority and side-effect receipts.
known: OpenConnector: 1,445 providers and 15,156 generated actions
Activepieces: mature pieces and connect-account UI
Nango and Jentic add provider/spec breadth
OpenConnector global connection storage failed tenancy requirements
open: Canonical provider/action schema?
Which popular providers need scripted setup?
How does browser operation fit?
What is the authority/approval model for side effects?
agent: Separate catalogue, OAuth engine, connection storage and action runtime; prove one tenant-safe connector flow.
latest_findings: Borrow OAuth machinery, catalogues, durable execution and authorization engines.
Own tenant-keyed connections, outbound token brokerage, idempotency, egress refusal and the action ledger.
Callers pass identity and intended action, never raw provider secrets.

title: Deterministic composition planner
thesis: Retrieve candidates, eliminate incompatible sets mechanically, then let AI choose among feasible plans and write only bounded glue.
known: Phase 8 selected plan-then-fill over monolithic generation
A model-free solver and 26 fixtures were designed
Blocks can be fitted without AI once contracts and bindings are explicit
open: What is the optimization objective?
When should a whole service beat several blocks?
Which fields are necessary for deterministic compatibility?
How should optional recommendations be presented to the client?
agent: Implement the model-free solver against synthetic service/module/package records and positive/negative fixtures.
latest_findings: Compose plan-then-fill: retrieve, eliminate incompatibilities deterministically, then let models choose among feasible options.
Deterministic systems own identity, authority, compatibility, dependency and evidence gates.
The composer must surface UNDERDETERMINED rather than invent compatibility.

title: Preview, editor and change loop
thesis: Clients need to alter the assembled product through conversation and direct visual controls without dissolving the composition back into arbitrary generated code.
known: The client should be able to pick side-nav/component variants and revise them in chat
Bounded edits against known assets are safer than free generation
Taste selection should happen before expensive code loops where possible
open: Which edits are parameter changes versus code changes?
How does the editor preserve block upgradeability?
What is the undo/version model?
How are unsupported requests explained?
agent: Define the editable surface and change taxonomy; prototype replace/add/remove/theme/text operations without arbitrary repo edits.
latest_findings: Persist typed edit intent instead of only code or DOM mutations.
Use denial-by-construction and record accepted, rejected and refused operations.
Puck shows field-level write authority can live in persisted data and survive upgrades.

title: Runtime, verification and release
thesis: Run heterogeneous capabilities in explicit profiles, verify the complete workflow, and release an exact recoverable composition.
owns: Build, contract, visual and workflow tests
known: A passing build is not client workflow proof
Different reuse shapes need different runtimes
Existing work defined receipt families and negative paths but admitted zero production blocks
open: Which runtime profiles are v1?
What sandbox/deploy infrastructure should be rented?
How are failures attributed per capability?
Can blocks upgrade independently?
agent: Define runtime profiles and prove one clean preview→workflow verification→release→rollback cycle.
latest_findings: Rollback is multi-object across artifact, configuration, data/schema and routing horizons.
Every capability needs stable identity, version, trace context, owner and machine-readable health.
ComputeSDK cannot be the load-bearing abstraction when memory-preserving pause is required.

title: Continuous corpus and production learning
thesis: Every new component, repository, conversion and production outcome should improve the shelf, taxonomy, recipes and future recommendations.
known: AutoSaaS already describes a procedural learning loop
Current corpus ranking is mostly metadata rather than production evidence
The remembered 1.3M/850k/80k corpus still lacks a current authoritative path
open: What production signals change ranking?
How often are component and repo sources refreshed?
How do we avoid taxonomy drift?
When is an asset deprecated or replaced?
agent: Define the evidence flywheel and ranking model using adaptation effort, workflow success, runtime burden and production history.
latest_findings: Consume edit, qualification, runtime, rollback and outcome receipts instead of inventing a parallel telemetry system.
Gate promotion on the weakest critical evidence family; never average away a fatal unknown.
Update capability ranking, reuse-shape choice, adaptation cost and retirement state from production evidence.
